summary: The web portal's memory showcase is now user-scoped — a logged-in person sees only their own Honcho representation, reversing the original v1 design where every whitelisted person's full memory was visible to everyone else on the list.
details: nora/web/memory.py's build_memory_payload now requires person_id and returns only that person's entry (an at-most-one-item list, same wire shape as before); a missing or unrecognized person_id returns [] rather than falling back to everyone's data.
app/src/app/api/memory/route.ts resolves the caller's own personId via checkSession() and passes it to Nora's /app/v1/memory as a query param.
2026-08-17-nora-web-design.md's original §2 non-goal ("no per-person opt-in/opt-out ... deliberate choice") is recorded as reversed, with the reasoning for why.
